title: Microsoft Purview Data Security Investigations: investigation notifications and query builder search
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, role-group controls, audit searches and consumption licensing are supported. It should narrow its statement that search never acts on content, preserve qualifications about notification recipients and AI preparation, and cite the supporting email and budget documentation.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Every item added to scope is prepared for AI analysis.
claims.quote: After data items are added to the investigation scope, the system automatically prepares all items. This automatic vectorization enables semantic searches and categorization of data.
claims.fix: Replace 'every item added to an investigation's scope is stored and prepared for AI analysis' with 'adding data to an investigation's scope incurs storage charges and can consume compute units for AI preparation'. In Cost and licensing, replace 'what is added to scope is stored and analysed under the meters above' with 'adding data to scope incurs storage charges and can consume compute units for AI preparation'. The scope page excludes previously vectorized items from revectorization and items without text from vectorization (https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-security-investigations-scope#automatic-vectorization).

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Data Security Investigations searches respect compliance boundaries configured with search permissions filters.
claims.quote: If your organization has configured compliance boundaries using search permissions filters, Data Security Investigations searches respect those boundaries.

claims.claim: Investigators scoped by a compliance boundary see results only for content locations within that boundary.
claims.quote: Investigators whose accounts are scoped by a compliance boundary only see search results for content locations within their permitted boundary.

claims.claim: Neither notifications nor the query builder takes action on content.
claims.quote: Searched: Data Security Investigations query builder notifications automatically take action content purge query. Read search and workflow pages and mitigation-actions purge excerpts; these describe query construction and separate purge execution, not this categorical exclusion.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'Notifications report events, and the query builder constructs search queries.' Remove 'No change' and 'neither takes action on content'; no source establishes that categorical claim.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Data Security Investigations uses consumption billing for stored data and AI capacity.
claims.quote: It uses pay-as-you-go and capacity billing models. This billing structure means you pay for the storage and AI capacity features you use in the solution.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Data Security Investigations is not billed on a dedicated enterprise plan or licence.
claims.quote: Billing in Data Security Investigations is based solely on the combination of the amount of stored data and the associated computing capacity needed for AI analysis. It isn't based on a dedicated enterprise plan or license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The pay-as-you-go storage meter bills per GB per month across all investigations.
claims.quote: The storage meter for Data Security Investigations uses the pay-as-you-go billing model. You pay for storage on a gigabyte (GB) per month basis for stored data associated with all investigations in your organization.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: AI analysis uses pay-as-you-go compute units.
claims.quote: Data Security Investigations uses the pay-as-you-go billing model for AI capacity. You need compute units for deep analysis and AI-related processing in your investigations. You pay only for the compute units you use.

claims.claim: Storage charges begin when items are added to investigation scope.
claims.quote: Data storage charges start when you add items to the scope of an investigation.

claims.claim: Cancelling an in-progress Add to scope, Categorization or Examination job does not remove charges for compute units already consumed.
claims.quote: If you cancel an in-progress job (such as Add to scope, Categorization, or Examination), you still pay for any compute units consumed before the cancellation.

claims.claim: The Usage dashboard shows storage and compute unit use per investigation.
claims.quote: Use the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard to quickly view and track data storage and compute unit usage for each investigation in your organization.

claims.claim: Only users assigned the Data Security Investigations Admin role can access the usage dashboard.
claims.quote: Only users assigned the Data Security Investigations Admin role can access the Pay-as-you-go usage dashboard.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends Azure budgets for the Data Security Investigations resource group.
claims.quote: Create budgets for the Data Security Investigations resource group and meter level.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends alerts as spending approaches budget thresholds.
claims.quote: Configure alerts when spending approaches defined thresholds (for example, 50%, 75%, or 90%).

claims.claim: Budget alerts notify about spending rather than stopping consumption.
claims.quote: Notifications are triggered when the budget thresholds are exceeded. Resources aren't affected, and your consumption isn't stopped.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/cost-management-billing/costs/tutorial-acm-create-budgets to sources for the statement that budget alerts do not stop consumption.
